model.title: National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act of 2025
model.meta: Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Ed Case (D-HI)

summary.text: The bill would create a National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Program run by the Secretary of the Interior through the Fish and Wildlife Service, to find and respond to priority invasive species threats on or near refuge lands and waters. It would set up at least one trained strike team in each Fish and Wildlife Service region, which would work on habitat restoration, prevention, early detection, rapid response, and management of invasive species, coordinating with governments, nonprofits, and private parties and sharing data through existing reporting systems. The Secretary could provide money, technical help, contracts, or grants to others dealing with invasive species near refuges, but responses on adjacent private or other lands would happen only at the owner's request. The Secretary would have to report to Congress and the public on the program two and five years after enactment, and the bill would authorize $10,000,000 per year for fiscal years 2027 through 2033.
